verses.1: And they said to him, “Man of Efraim, what have you done to us? Why do you call us to battle when you yourself went to fight against Midian? They fought against him with great strength.”
verses.2: And he said to them, “What have I done now? How can I be considered good when I have caused such suffering to my people? I am a tyrant who causes harm to others.”
verses.3: In your hands, God has placed the leaders of Midian, Eber and Zebulun. What I can do, I will do. Then their spirit departed from them through their words.
verses.4: And Gideon came out of the Jordan, past those three men who were sick and weak.
verses.5: And he said to the people of Sukkot, “Please give them bread as food for the people who are tired and weak. For I am in pursuit of sacrifices, and I am distracted by the kings of Midian.”
verses.6: And the priests said, “Now, you must hold this offering and this sacrificial offering in your hands, as if it were bread given to your army.”
verses.7: And Gideon said to them, “Let the offerings and the sacrifices be offered before Jehovah. I will also use my spear to pierce their flesh, along with the edges of their armor and their shields.”
verses.8: And Penuel went up there, and he spoke to them in this manner. The people of Penuel answered him just as the people of Sihon had answered.
verses.9: And he said to the people of Penuel, “When I return, I will destroy that great tower.”
verses.10: And they offered sacrifices and burnt offerings in the morning. Their camps were filled with forty thousand people from all the camps of the Israelites. There were also one hundred and twenty thousand people who were killed as sacrifices.
verses.11: And Gideon led his men along the roads to the camps that had been set up there before. He destroyed those camps. The camps were in a state of disrepair.
verses.12: And Zebah and Zilek followed them. They captured both kings of Midian: Zebah and Zilek, along with all their troops.
verses.13: And Gideon, son of Joash, returned from the battlefield, from the site of the destruction.
verses.14: And he called a young man from among the people of Sukkot. He asked him to write down the names of Sukkot’s leaders and their ages: seventy-seven men in total.
verses.15: And he went before the people of Sukkot and said, “Look, here is a burnt offering and a grain offering that will bring them shame. Now, hold these offerings in your hands, for they are given to your people who are going to be eaten by worms.”
verses.16: And he took the elders of the city, along with those who lived by the sea, and also the barkspersons. He learned from them about the people of Sukoth.
verses.17: And he destroyed the tower of Penuel, and killed the people of that city.
verses.18: And he said to Zebakh and Tzalmunah, “Where are the people you killed in the ditch?” They replied, “Just like them, they’re all the same. They’re just like the sons of the king.”
verses.19: And he said, “My brothers, these are the children of my mother. They are the people of Jehovah. I did not kill you.”
verses.20: And he said to Yeter in his cage, “Get up and kill them.” But the boy did not throw away his weapon out of fear that he might still be considered a boy.
verses.21: And Zephath and Tzalmunah said, “Stand up! You will harm us, for you are a powerful man.” Then Gideon rose up and killed Zephath and Tzalmunah. He also took away the silver coins that were in their chests.
verses.22: And the people of Israel said to Gideon, “You too, and your sons, and your grandsons, for you have saved us from the hands of Midian.”
verses.23: And Gadon said to them, “I will not rule over you. Nor will I rule over your children. But Jehovah will rule over you.”
verses.24: And Gideon said to them, “I will ask a question of you. Give me one man who can blow the trumpet for me, so that I can use it as a signal for them. Then they will listen.”
verses.25: And they said, “Nathan, give it to me.” Then they unwrapped the shawl and threw it aside. Each person took their share of it.
verses.26: And he measured the gold that was requested: one thousand seven hundred talents of gold alone, from all the gold that was stored in the treasuries and from the ornaments that belonged to the kings of Media. This was also part of the gold that was used to make the crowns for their heads.
verses.27: And Gideon made it into an altar for worship. He displayed it in his city, on a hilltop. All of Israel went there after him. Thus, Gideon and his house became famous among the people.
verses.28: And Midian submitted before the children of Israel. They were unable to carry their heads on their shoulders. The land was in chaos for forty years during the time of Gideon.
verses.29: And Jirubael, son of Yoash, went and sat in his house.
verses.30: And in Ligdun, there were seventy sons. They were born from his penis, because he had many daughters.
verses.31: And Pilagsho, who was born in Shechem, was also a son. He gave him the name Avimelach.
verses.32: And Gideon, son of Joash, died in a good death. He was buried alongside his father Joash, at Mount Abi’ei.
verses.33: And when Gideon died, the children of Israel returned and followed their husbands. They made them gods to worship.
verses.34: And the children of Israel did not remember Jehovah their God, who saved them from all their enemies around them.
verses.35: And they did not show any kindness to the house of Jerubbaal Gidion, as they did all the good things they did to Israel.
